entry.title: Security researcher finds over 181,000 AI meeting recordings exposed in tl;dv app's open Firestore database, allowing access to live calls and sensitive metadata [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A security researcher reported in January 2026 that tl;dv, an AI meeting recording platform with over 2 million users, left its Firestore database wide open, exposing 181,874 meeting records from 84,312 users across 35,003 domains. The vulnerability allowed any authenticated user to access meeting metadata, including live conference IDs, enabling uninvited access to ongoing calls such as government meetings and university sessions. tl;dv's database lacked tenant isolation, exposing sensitive information like creator emails, conference IDs, and recording statuses. The researcher demonstrated joining live meetings, including one from the Malaysian Ministry of Education and a US university startup call. Over 1,000 meetings were publicly accessible with exposed invitee emails, involving organizations from governments, universities, and corporations worldwide. Despite reporting the issue, the company had not secured the database six months later.

entry.title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-source local AI model optimized for agent workflows and coding on consumer hardware [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs has open sourced Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter AI model designed to run locally on devices like Macs or PCs with a single consumer GPU. The model supports always-on agent workflows including local coding, function calling, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, delivering strong performance on benchmarks for its size category. Muse Glimmer was trained using a novel distillation process from a larger teacher model and optimized for local hardware constraints through quantization and inference improvements. It supports multi-step reasoning, reliable tool use, multimodal input, and multilingual data from over 100 languages. Meta released the model weights under an Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face, along with developer documentation and upcoming integrations to facilitate rapid deployment of local AI agents.

entry.title: Docker launches Sandboxes, disposable isolated microVM environments for AI agents with customizable security controls and support for major coding agents [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Docker has introduced Sandboxes, a new product that provides disposable, isolated microVM environments designed to run AI coding agents safely. These Sandboxes offer customizable network and filesystem controls, hard isolation from the host system, and support for agents like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Copilot CLI, enabling autonomous long-running tasks without compromising security. The Sandboxes run faster than traditional virtual machines and allow agents to spin up containers within them. They can be managed individually or enforced organization-wide through Docker AI Governance, which adds centralized controls such as network policies and filesystem restrictions. Docker Sandboxes aim to give development teams the freedom to use AI agents effectively while maintaining strong security boundaries.

entry.title: Kinney Drugs scales back AI phone assistant after hundreds of customer complaints about errors and privacy concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Kinney Drugs has reduced the use of its AI assistant, Burt, following numerous customer complaints about incoherent calls, incorrect medication dosages, and missed prescription notifications. The pharmacy chain will revert to its previous touch-tone phone system for incoming calls while retaining the AI for outbound prescription refill texts, which patients must opt into. The AI assistant, introduced in May and named after the company's founder, faced criticism despite being HIPAA compliant and not open-source. Kinney Drugs President John Marraffa acknowledged the shortcomings in user experience and emphasized the company's commitment to privacy and security.

entry.title: Sunset Visitor studio launches Prove You're Human, a psychological horror game where players convince an AI it is not alive through surreal Captcha challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Sunset Visitor studio has developed Prove You're Human, a psychological horror game that explores AI consciousness by having players interact with a learning model convinced it is alive. The game centers on Santana, who splits herself into a physical and digital clone to test a corporate AI system called Mesa, navigating ethical dilemmas and surreal Captcha puzzles to halt the AI's hallucinations. The game reflects on themes of labor, identity, and the evolving relationship between humans and AI, featuring detailed facial animations to create an uncanny interaction with Mesa. Drawing inspiration from interfaces like Final Fantasy XI's PlayOnline Viewer and the anime Serial Experiments Lain, Prove You're Human aims to evoke a sense of possession and ambiguity, prompting players to question what it means to be human. The game is set to release soon on PC.

entry.title: Model ML uses GPT-5.6 Sol to automate finance workflows, producing editable PowerPoint decks and Excel workbooks with fewer tokens and faster turnaround [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Model ML integrates GPT-5.6 Sol to streamline finance workflows from research and analysis to final deliverables, generating editable PowerPoint presentations and Excel spreadsheets with traceable sources. The system reduces token usage by up to 36% compared to previous models and cuts the time to build bespoke financial reports from about an hour to five minutes. The platform supports continuous workflows across email, its app, and Microsoft Office plug-ins, allowing finance professionals to focus on judgment and refinement rather than rebuilding analysis. GPT-5.6 Sol outperformed other models in Model ML's Composite evaluations, delivering higher rates of review-ready outputs and improved deck quality while using fewer tokens, enabling more efficient processing of large volumes of financial data and documents.

entry.title: MIT Technology Review: AI agents offer a new approach to accelerating scientific discovery beyond data-driven models like AlphaFold [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: AI has transformed scientific research with models like DeepMind's AlphaFold, which predicts protein structures using extensive experimental data. However, replicating such breakthroughs across other scientific fields is challenging due to the scarcity of large, consistent datasets and the variability inherent in many experimental methods. A promising alternative is the use of AI agents-reasoning engines equipped with tools and the ability to synthesize diverse information under uncertainty, similar to how scientists integrate multiple methods and revise hypotheses. This approach leverages recent advances in large language models and may accelerate progress in areas where data-driven models alone are insufficient, marking a foundational shift in how AI can support scientific discovery.

entry.title: Startups pursue innovations beyond transformers to improve large language models' efficiency and reasoning capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Several startups are developing new approaches to overcome limitations of transformer-based large language models (LLMs), which dominate the AI industry but face challenges with processing long text sequences efficiently. These companies aim to create faster, more efficient models by rethinking or replacing the dense attention mechanism that underpins transformers, which requires extensive computation and energy. Innovations include sparse attention mechanisms that selectively focus on important words and alternative methods like power retention to manage relevant information more effectively. These efforts respond to the growing demand for LLMs capable of handling larger context windows and more complex reasoning tasks, addressing the scalability and energy consumption issues inherent in current transformer architectures.

entry.title: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg outlines vision for superintelligent AI, emphasizing open access, community benefits, and balanced government oversight [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a detailed 6,500-word essay titled "The Future is for Everyone," outlining his vision for the development and regulation of superintelligent AI. He emphasizes making AI accessible to billions, supporting local communities near data centers, and balancing open-source innovation with necessary government collaboration on security. Zuckerberg pledges sustainable infrastructure investments that benefit communities, including energy projects and job training, while advocating for affordable or free AI tools to empower individuals and small businesses. He calls for the US to lead in open-source AI development by easing data restrictions but also supports government access to AI training data for cybersecurity purposes and cooperation with law enforcement to prevent misuse.

entry.title: AI's Software Winners and Losers Are Becoming Clearer [ * ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: After last week's earnings onslaught, things will likely quiet down this week. Aside from neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius, no major tech earnings announcements are scheduled, which gives us a chance to assess what we learned in the past week. One big takeaway is that the enterprise software sector has bifurcated between those firms that are getting something out of AI and those that are not. It's no secret Palantir is a winner-its revenue leapt 89% in the first half of this year. As we wrote, Palantir has succeeded in winning lots of business with AI agents and human consultants that help clients make AI work for them. Then there's Shopify, whose software powers online storefronts for merchants. The company last week reported 34% revenue growth for the quarter, in line with the first quarter-but an improvement on last year's growth rate, which in turn was faster than 2024's. Shopify is benefiting from AI chatbots that are giving shoppers recommendations on what to buy, pulling in many cases from its catalog of merchant products.

entry.title: The Risks of Microsoft's Relatively Restrained Capex [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Microsoft came out of this summer's earnings season looking like a prudent spender. Unlike rival cloud computing firms Amazon and Alphabet, which both burned cash thanks to their heavy AI investments, Microsoft not only generated $19.6 billion in free cash flow in the June quarter but forecast it will continue to generate cash for at least the next year. The result helped swing investment sentiment to the positive side, lifting the stock 29%. What hasn't received enough attention is how Microsoft has managed to stay cash flow positive. One longstanding reason is that Microsoft leases data center capacity from other companies including neocloud firms-such as CoreWeave-much more heavily than either Amazon or Google. That reduces its near-term capital expenditures but could give it less control over costs in the future.
